newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan cement concern listed, targets institutions.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan cement concern listed, targets institutions.

text.p: An Initial Public Offer of shares in family cement firm Athi River Mining Company began on Thursday targetted at institutional investors, brokers said.

Some 15.728 million shares are on offer to the public at a price of 12.25 shillings (21 cents) each. Of these, 11 million shares or 70 percent are reserved for institutional investors while the remaining 4.7 million shares will be given to individuals.

"It's very very important for us that this issue succeeds because then we will see more Asian companies listed on the stock exchange," John Munge, managing director of sponsoring brokers Shah, Munge & Partners, told Reuters.
There are many thriving businesses owned by investors of Asian origin in Kenya. Most have shunned the stock exchange partly for fear of losing control.
Athi River's is the second initial public offering in the year after Tourism Promotion Services, the trading name of leading hotel concern Serena Lodges and Hotels Ltd.
Athi River's announcement that it would use about 40 percent of the funds raised from the offer to offset an outstanding loan cast a shadow on the offer and dampened speculator interest.
The company prospectus says Athi River hopes to raise 281.75 million shillings by selling 23 million shares. It will use 110 million shillings to repay a portion of its long-term debt.

"It will take about three years before investors begin seeing any sort of returns. If I was an investor, I'd buy it and forget about it for some time," said Kamalesh Kantaria, managing director of brokerage firm Bond & Equity.
Long-term returns is the main reason the company aims to tap institutional investors.
"By transferring the company's debt to equity, the company will save about 45 million shillings on interest costs alone in 1997 and 1998," said Sejal Pattni of brokers Ashbu Securities.
Munge said the company's strength lay in the fact that besides cement production, it had diversified into manufacture of industrial chemicals and minerals.
Cement production is the company's core business and accounts for 60 percent of turnover while industrial minerals and chemicals account for 19 and 21 percent respectively.
Athi River posted after-tax profits in 1996 at 28.147 million shillings from 18.78 million in 1995. They forecast such profits to reach 46.2 million shillings in 1997.
The firm will be the third cement company quoted on the NSE after Bamburi Cement and East African Portland Cement and the 58th listed company on the bourse.
